title: Refuting the QAOA fixed-angle conjecture
abstract: The fixed-angle conjecture for the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA) is shown to be false for depth-2 QAOA on 9-regular graphs, and proven to be correct for depth-1 on any regular graph, as well, as for any depth on all 2-regular graphs.
summary: This paper rigorously analyzes the fixed-angle conjecture for QAOA applied to MaxCut, a key problem in quantum optimization. It proves the conjecture holds for shallow depths or low-degree graphs, but crucially refutes it by providing a counterexample on the 9-regular graph $K_{9,9}$ at depth $p=2$. This refutation refines the theoretical understanding of when and how QAOA performance scales with graph structure.
main_problem: The paper investigates and refutes the fixed-angle conjecture concerning the performance of the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm (QAOA) for solving the MaxCut problem.
main_result: The fixed-angle conjecture is proven false for depth-2 QAOA on 9-regular graphs, while it is confirmed to be true for depth-1 on any regular graph and for all depths on 2-regular graphs.
method: The analysis uses theoretical bounds derived from the structure of the QAOA expectation value, comparing performance on general graphs to optimized tree structures, and employs advanced techniques like symmetry-adapted bases and tensor product factorization.
model_or_system: The model is the QAOA applied to the MaxCut problem, formulated using an Ising encoding Hamiltonian $H_f$ on $d$-regular graphs, particularly focusing on complete bipartite graphs $K_{d,d}$.
key_observables: The approximation ratio $C( eta, \gamma) = F( eta, \gamma) / C_{\max}$, and the difference $\delta_e$ between the tree-optimal objective value and the edge expectation value.
important_parameters: QAOA depth ($p$), graph regularity ($d$), and the graph structure (e.g., $K_{9,9}$ for the counterexample).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the locality property of QAOA, which restricts correlations to a distance $p$ on the graph.
figures_summary: Figure 1 illustrates the tree structure $T_{p}^d$ used for comparison. Figure 2 shows complete bipartite graphs $K_{d,d}$ up to $d=9$, highlighting $K_{9,9}$ as the counterexample for $p=2$.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the context of the conjecture, then proves its validity for specific cases ($p=1$ and $d \le 2$), and finally presents a rigorous counterexample for $p=2$ on $K_{9,9}$ by analyzing the expectation values in a symmetry-adapted basis.
why_interesting: This work directly impacts the theoretical understanding of quantum algorithms for combinatorial optimization, providing concrete counterexamples that challenge existing assumptions about parameter optimization in QAOA.

figures.caption: FIG. 1. The tree T p d is built from a centre edge ij (red) by including every vertex within graph distance p of i or j in a d-regular graph G of girth ≥2(p +1). Edges and vertices are shaded by their graph distance to the centre edge, from saturated blue at distance 1, i.e., T 1 d , to faded grey at distance 3; the latter lie outside T 2 d , and the dashed stubs indicate that G extends even further. Shown are d = 3 on the left, and d = 4 on the right.

FIG. 2. The complete bipartite graphs Kd,d for d = 1, 2, 3, . . . , 9; every vertex in one part is joined to every vertex in the other part, so each edge lies in (d −1)2 four-cycles. K9,9 serves as a counterexample to the fixed-angle conjecture for p = 2 on 9-regular graphs.
